question.text: Which of the following is NOT an Event-driven Investment Strategy as per Section 10.1.4 of the chapter?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 10.1.4 lists Activist/Special-Situations, Merger Arbitrage and Pre-IPO under Event-driven. Market-Neutral is Section 10.1.1.3, an Equity-Market strategy — NOT event-driven; it relies on stock mispricing, not a specific corporate event. **The Trap:** All three event-driven options (A, B, C) are listed in the PDF; market-neutral (D) is equity-market. Students often conflate 'any long-short' with 'event-driven', which is wrong. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers the same taxonomy. XIX-D (Cat I/II) event-driven is limited to distressed PE/NCLT plays — a different universe. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Event-driven alpha is 'binary' — it fires on a catalyst. Budget your sleeve to run 30-50 concurrent positions to avoid single-deal break risk wiping the year's return. Risk-budget by deal-break VaR, not by notional.
